text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- University of Zambia chancellor Andrew Siwela has rejected allegations of mismanagement and embezzlement against his administration, and in turn blamed the government for ongoing student unrest at the institution.
- President Frederick Chiluba condemned the violence in Congo, saying the warring parties should have waited for elections scheduled for next month to settle their differences.
- The Economic Association of Zambia said a 24 percent fuel price increase coming into effect this week would distort the economy.
- The association also said Zambia's total exports fell by 19.5 percent last year.
- Police in Lusaka arrested 11 striking University Teaching Hospital workers and charged them with conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace.

- A witness in an electoral petition challenging the outcome of general elecitons last November told the Supreme Court that results in some areas showed totals greater than the number of registered voters.
- Former president Kenneth Kaunda is scheduled to meet Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe to seek Southern African Development Community help in ending Zambia's political crisis.
